svg.text: Recursive partitioning of sorted read begins
At an internal node there are two sorted sequences: the boundary keys between children and the begins of the reads routed to the node. Instead of searching
the boundaries once per read, the algorithm partitions both sequences together: pick the middle boundary, split the reads around it, recurse on each side.
four children, so three boundaries; five reads sorted by begin
lower_bound(40) over the read begins: first begin ≥ 40
compare 1 middle read 40: 40 ≥ 40 → keep searching to the left (equality does not stop the search)
compare 2 middle read 25: 25 < 40 → the split is between 25 and 40
Two comparisons. Equal begins go to the right: with duplicates of 40 in the sequence, all of them
must land in the child whose minimum is 40, so an equal read cannot end a lower-bound search early.
boundary 40 is resolved and appears in neither subproblem
an empty side creates no subproblem;
reads with no boundary left belong to one child
One more partition on each side resolves 20 and 60. These are child destinations at one node, not leaves; each nonempty group repeats the procedure
inside its child. Partitioning uses begins only: a read is not truncated at a boundary, and its scan may later continue past the child it was routed to.
Routing comparisons in this example, and in general
Independent searches, standard upper_bound over the 3 boundaries without an equality shortcut: 2 comparisons per read, 10 in total.
Recursive partitioning: 2 comparisons to split around 40, then 2 to resolve 20 over [10, 25] and 2 to resolve 60 over [40, 45, 70]: 6 comparisons.
With k boundaries and k sorted reads: independent searches cost O(k log k) comparisons; recursive partitioning costs O(k). In general the bound is
O(m log(1 + M/m)) with m = min(boundaries, reads) and M = max: with one read it is still O(log k); with many more reads than boundaries, whole slices are classified at once.
These are routing key comparisons at one node, with the input already sorted. They exclude sorting, variable-length byte compares, expired-separator
repair and the interval scans that follow; they are not an elapsed-time speedup. Tasks, suspension and prefetching are described in the next figures.
